name: Surabaya
meta_description: TDSC investigative consulting in matters touching Surabaya: supplier diligence, asset research and insolvency support in East Java's port and industry hub.
hero_lede: Surabaya is the capital of East Java, Indonesia's second city and the commercial gateway to the eastern archipelago through the port of Tanjung Perak. TDSC scopes investigative consulting for matters running through the city from Nashville, coordinating Indonesian counsel and qualified local professionals where local work is required.
intro: Surabaya is the capital of East Java and Indonesia's second-largest city, with about 3.0 million residents in mid-2025 according to BPS estimates and a wider metropolitan region of roughly ten million across Gresik, Sidoarjo and neighbouring regencies. It has long been described as the gateway to the east: the port of Tanjung Perak is the centre of inter-island shipping for eastern Indonesia and ranks second nationally after Jakarta's Tanjung Priok. Trade, manufacturing, hospitality, construction and logistics dominate the city's output, and groups such as Sampoerna, Maspion, Wings, Pakuwon, Jawa Pos and the state shipbuilder PAL Indonesia are associated with the city.

Organisations commission investigative work connected to Surabaya because it is where many East Java manufacturers, commodity traders and inter-island shipping lines are owned and managed. Buyers sourcing food products, tobacco, furniture, electronics and household goods need to know who stands behind their suppliers. Lenders and investors face family-controlled groups whose holdings span Surabaya, Sidoarjo and Gresik, and creditors increasingly use the Surabaya Commercial Court for bankruptcy and debt-suspension (PKPU) proceedings. Shipping and logistics companies serving Kalimantan, Sulawesi and eastern Indonesia from Surabaya also bring counterparty, cargo and fraud exposure that cross-border clients want examined.

matters.title: East Java supplier and manufacturer diligence
matters.text: Foreign buyers sourcing processed food, furniture, tobacco products and household goods from Surabaya and its industrial hinterland verify ownership, production capacity, subcontracting, permits and litigation before contracting, and check whether a supplier's group has been through PKPU or bankruptcy proceedings.

matters.title: Family group ownership mapping
matters.text: Surabaya business groups often hold manufacturing, property and trading companies through relatives and affiliated entities across Sidoarjo, Gresik and Jakarta. Work reconstructs control from Ministry of Law company data, court decisions and Indonesian-language press, noting where nominee arrangements prevent full documentation.

matters.title: Insolvency and PKPU creditor support
matters.text: Creditors facing a debtor in PKPU before the Surabaya Commercial Court need to know what assets, affiliates and receivables exist and whether transfers preceded the filing. Research supports claims verification, voting on composition plans and decisions on whether to seek bankruptcy instead.

matters.title: Shipping line and logistics counterparties
matters.text: Surabaya is headquarters to major domestic shipping lines and many forwarders serving eastern Indonesia. Diligence on vessel operators, agents and warehouse companies covers ownership, fleet, claims history and disputes, supporting charter, cargo insurance and logistics partnership decisions.

matters.title: Property developer and land reviews
matters.text: Investors and lenders in Surabaya's residential, retail and industrial property markets review developers' land titles, permits, project delivery record and consumer or contractor disputes, which frequently surface in local court decisions and regional press before they appear in national reporting.

local_context.title: Surabaya Commercial Court
local_context.text: The Commercial Court (Pengadilan Niaga) in Surabaya sits within the Surabaya District Court and is a specialised chamber of the general courts. It hears bankruptcy and PKPU applications under Law No. 37 of 2004, along with intellectual property and other commercial matters, for parties in its region. Decisions carry case numbers ending PN.Niaga.Sby, such as a 2023 PKPU settled by composition, and published decisions are a useful source on a group's financial distress and creditors.

local_context.title: Surabaya District Court
local_context.text: Ordinary civil claims, including contract disputes, unlawful act claims and enforcement, are heard at the Surabaya District Court (Pengadilan Negeri Surabaya), with appeals to the East Java High Court. Execution of judgments still follows the HIR and RBg procedural rules. Court decisions published online let researchers identify prior litigation involving Surabaya companies and their owners, though coverage is incomplete and searches need to be run in Indonesian.

local_context.title: Port of Tanjung Perak
local_context.text: Tanjung Perak is operated by the state port company Pelindo and covers a development area of about 1,574 hectares in Pabean Cantian, north Surabaya. Its container terminal, Terminal Petikemas Surabaya, has been a joint venture with DP World. In cargo, customs and fraud matters, identifying which terminal, operator, shipping line and agent handled a consignment is the starting point for locating documents and witnesses.

local_context.title: Company and permit records
local_context.text: Companies in Surabaya are registered nationally through the Ministry of Law's legal administration system and licensed through the Online Single Submission platform, as described on our Indonesia page. City-specific work adds Surabaya and East Java court decisions, regional business press such as Jawa Pos, and local land office enquiries made through Indonesian counsel or a notary where a lawful basis exists.

tdsc_approach: For Surabaya matters TDSC first maps which entities sit in the city, which sit in neighbouring Sidoarjo or Gresik, and which are held in Jakarta or offshore. Research draws on Indonesian company data available through lawful channels, published Surabaya court and commercial court decisions, port and shipping information, and Indonesian- and Javanese-language reporting reviewed by native speakers. Where site visits to factories, interviews or retrieval of land and court documents are needed, TDSC coordinates qualified local professionals and works under the direction of the client's Indonesian counsel, in line with Indonesia's personal data protection law. Every counterparty is screened for sanctions exposure, and reports distinguish documented facts from local reputation.

faqs.q: Why does Surabaya matter for supply chain diligence?
faqs.a: Surabaya and its surrounding regencies form one of Indonesia's largest manufacturing regions, producing food, tobacco, furniture, electronics and household goods. Many exporters, and the family groups that own them, are managed from the city, so ownership, litigation and reputational information about East Java suppliers is usually found there and in its courts.

faqs.q: Which court handles bankruptcy cases involving Surabaya companies?
faqs.a: Bankruptcy and PKPU (suspension of debt payment) applications are heard by the Commercial Court in Surabaya, which sits within the Surabaya District Court and applies Law No. 37 of 2004. Its decisions are published with case numbers ending PN.Niaga.Sby and can reveal a debtor's creditors, assets and restructuring history.

faqs.q: How important is the port of Tanjung Perak?
faqs.a: Tanjung Perak is Indonesia's second-busiest port after Tanjung Priok and the centre of inter-island shipping for eastern Indonesia. Goods moving between Java and Kalimantan, Sulawesi, Bali, Nusa Tenggara and Papua frequently pass through it, which makes its operators, agents and shipping lines relevant in cargo, trade and fraud matters.

faqs.q: Can company ownership in Surabaya be fully documented?
faqs.a: Often only in part. Company data and beneficial ownership disclosures exist at national level, but family groups commonly use relatives and nominees, and some records require a lawful basis or counsel to obtain. Court decisions and local press help, but reports should say clearly where control is inferred rather than documented.

faqs.q: Does TDSC have an office in Surabaya?
faqs.a: No. TDSC is based in Nashville, Tennessee and has no office or staff in Indonesia. Engagements touching Surabaya are scoped and managed from Nashville. Where local work is needed, TDSC coordinates qualified Indonesian professionals and works with the client's Indonesian counsel, and does not claim any Indonesian licence.
